title: Enterprise GPU lanes: SLA tiers, soft-cap overage, and autoscale experiments
creator: Marco Liu
description:
Context:
Large enterprise prospects are asking for predictable throughput SLAs but also want flexibility for occasional spikes. Existing reserved models are too rigid for some customers and additive burst credits create complexity during contracting. This ticket scopes a set of experiments to evaluate a new 'GPU lane' packaging concept: fixed throughput lanes with soft-cap overage, explicit autoscale bands, and tiered SLA guarantees.

Goals:
- Design packaging that balances predictable revenue (multi-month commitment) with an easy-to-understand overage model for spikes.
- Measure impact on conversion for Enterprise RFPs and average revenue per account (ARPA).
- Ensure contract/legal and security questionnaire answers align to offer (KMS, network isolation, audit logs).
- Build a billing prototype and console UI for lanes and soft-cap metrics.

Proposed experiment variants (A/B):
A) Lanes + Soft-Cap Credits: Customers buy named throughput lane(s) (e.g., 1k TPS-equivalent) with a 10% soft-cap per month that incurs progressive overage pricing. Overage throttles only after 110% sustained for >5 minutes.
B) Lanes + Autoscale Bands: Same lanes but with autoscale window that temporarily provisions burst capacity up to N lanes at Xx cost/hour; customer is billed for extra lanes used. Adds explicit burst visibility in the console.
C) Hybrid Commitment: Lower base price for longer commitment (12 mo) + cheaper soft-cap rate and pre-paid buffer credits.

Key design trade-offs discussed:
- Predictability vs flexibility: Soft-cap preserves predictable committed revenue while allowing short spikes; pricing must not cannibalize Dedicated reserved contracts.
- Enforcement mechanism: Prefer delayed throttling with billing-based guardrails vs instantaneous hard throttles to reduce customer surprises.
- Sales experience: Contracts need clear language around overage smoothing, measurement window, and auditability of metering.

Success metrics:
- +15% lift in enterprise trial-to-contract conversion for customers requiring SLA clarity within 3 months of pilot.
- <5% churn risk triggered by unexpected overage invoices (tracked via NPS + billing dispute rate).
- Observable reduction in committed-instance provisioning time during peaks (SLO: 95th pct improvement vs baseline).

Operational requirements:
- Metering: per-lane token/TPS accounting, 1-minute rollups, retention for 365 days for audits.
- Billing: support progressive overage tiers and pre-paid buffer redemption. Finance to provide invoice prototype.
- Console: new 'Lanes' page showing soft-cap utilization, forecasted overage, and autoscale history. UX to include opt-in toggle for autoscale bands.
- Legal/Sec: update standard MSA & SOW templates to describe soft-cap behavior; complete enterprise security questionnaire (SOC/KMS/Audit) snippet for lane offering.

Open questions / risks:
- Pricing elasticity: Will soft-cap pricing depress full reserved sales? (Mitigation: run on a small cohort of segmented customers and cap enrollments.)
- Complexity for sales: Might increase negotiation time; need 1-pager and pricing calculator for AE use.
- Implementation effort: Metering + billing changes estimated as medium-high (dependency ENG-88512).
